podcast.body: The concluding track of the "Sargent Pepper" album, famously incorporating a dog whistle into its run-out groove. This recording, which only canines could detect, caused dogs to become agitated and would play indefinitely due to being in a locked groove. "When a day in the life ended off the Sargent Pepper album in 1967, dogs went nuts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The final chord of this iconic song served as the direct inspiration for the welcome sound designed by Jim Riggs for the Apple Mac 4 in the early 1990s. This choice aimed to create a satisfying and memorable startup experience for users. "Adegin de Life."

podcast.body: This John Lennon masterpiece, the final track from The Beatles' 'Sgt. Pepper's' album, was referenced lyrically in the middle of David Bowie's song "Young Americans." The reference was vocalized by Bowie's Luther Vandross-led chorus, creating an "improbable Beatles connection." "Boey drops a lyrical reference to the final track from the Beatles' Sergeant Pepper album, the John Lennon masterpiece, A Day in the Life."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
